exercise.name: Superman

reference.title: Superman (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

exercise.mechanics: Isometric hold with a short lift (trunk and hip extension)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you lift, keep breathing lightly in the hold, inhale as you lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 2 s hold, 1 s down, 1 s rest

prescription.tempo: 1 s up, 2 s hold, 1 s down
prescription.progression: Longer holds (5-10 s), then alternating arm and leg lifts or back extensions on a bench

cues.text: Lie face down, arms straight overhead, legs straight, forehead just off the mat.
Squeeze the glutes and lift the arms, chest and legs a few centimetres off the mat.
Hold about 2 s, reaching long through the fingers and toes; look at the mat.
Lower slowly back to the mat.
Relax for a moment, then repeat.

mistakes.fix: Keep the neck long; eyes on the mat.
Lift only a few centimetres; length, not height.
Keep the legs straight and lift from the hips.

kinematics.norm: A few centimetres off the mat (clinical opinion)
A few centimetres off the mat (clinical opinion)
Small; the lift loads the lumbar spine with about 4,000 N or more of compression in the full superman (McGill 1998)
A few degrees past neutral, knees straight (clinical opinion)
Arms overhead in line with the body, lifted slightly (clinical opinion)
About 2 s hold at the top (clinical opinion)

sources.title: McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765)
Callaghan, Gunning and McGill 1998, the relationship between lumbar spine load and muscle activity during extensor exercises (Phys Ther 78(1):8-18)
Kim et al. 2014, selective activation of lumbar paraspinal muscles during exercises in the prone position (J Phys Ther Sci 26(8):1223-1224)
Kelly et al. 2016, lumbar iliocostalis and lumbar multifidus EMG during stabilization exercises in prone, quadruped and sitting positions (J Phys Ther Sci 28(10):2950-2954)
Dafkou et al. 2021, lumbar multifidus thickness during graded quadruped and prone exercises (Int J Exerc Sci 14(7):101-112)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Low back pain, spondylolisthesis or spinal stenosis: the full superman has high spine compression (about 4,000-6,000 N, McGill 1998); use the bird dog or single-limb lifts instead.
Neck pain: keep the head down.
modify: Lift only the arms and chest, or only the legs.
Alternate: lift one arm and the opposite leg (lower load).
regressions: Bird dog (quadruped opposite arm and leg).
progressions: Back extension on a bench or Roman chair.

muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Lift and hold the chest and legs. Prone trunk extension gave the highest lumbar paraspinal activity of the prone and quadruped exercises tested (Kim 2014: about 50% MVIC; Kelly 2016). A cited study put the full superman at about 62-82% MVC (Dafkou 2021 review).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_l: Lift and hold the chest and legs. Prone trunk extension gave the highest lumbar paraspinal activity of the prone and quadruped exercises tested (Kim 2014: about 50% MVIC; Kelly 2016). A cited study put the full superman at about 62-82% MVC (Dafkou 2021 review).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Extends the hips to lift the legs.
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Extends the hips to lift the legs.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Help extend the hips with the knees straight.
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Help extend the hips with the knees straight.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Set the shoulder blades as the arms lift overhead (the lower trapezius does most of this; clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_l: Set the shoulder blades as the arms lift overhead (the lower trapezius does most of this; clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Helps hold the arms up off the mat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Helps hold the arms up off the mat (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Centres the shoulder with the arms overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Centres the shoulder with the arms overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Abdominals stay lightly braced so the lift comes from the whole back, not a sharp low-back hinge (clinical opinion).
